title: Make a review loop converge
statement: In a repeated review loop, act only on findings that show harm rather than preference, keep earlier decisions unless new evidence arrives, and pause after a round with nothing critical.
detail: The reading project's quality rules name oscillation as the failure mode of an unsupervised improve-loop, each round fixing what the round before chose. So a finding must prove harm, not preference; recorded decisions are immutable inside the loop, and a later round may escalate a deferred item only with new evidence; and a round with zero critical findings pauses the loop. Its change-control baseline adds that recency, confidence and citation count do not supersede an earlier decision and holds a change of direction for one consolidated decision, and a later review brief downgrades a pattern already in the signed baseline to a note unless it actively harms the child.
against: Treating earlier decisions as settled does not resolve two reviews that genuinely conflict: one had asked for a frame that the other proposed replacing, and that conflict was held for a consolidated decision (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0218-devfactory-review-and-decision-brief-2026-09-10.qmd`, lines 74-77).

Improvements need an existing acceptance criterion plus a demonstrated defect; speculative polish, additional grades and repeated redesign are excluded.
Recency and strength of wording are not approval.

Requiring every goal to appear first would be an unsupported design rule and could defeat the explicit source-first order. A later change needs actual learner evidence or a deliberate teaching decision, not a broad expansion of `goalCheckShape`.
Findings ONLY where something is genuinely wrong for the child — no style opinions, no "could be nicer", no restating mech noise you could not confirm on the screenshot.
They are not a reason to discard existing work or reopen settled creative decisions.
POLISH items are never auto-fixed. A zero-CRITICAL round pauses the loop.
A reviewer objection should identify which rule is violated… otherwise, it is a new preference or scope change.
